identified_convention.reading: The contract's exclusion rule is member_class != 'base' (28 members). The panel also carries a renderer field whose 'chatml' value selects a DIFFERENT 26-member subset. Whichever quoted values are reproduced only under the renderer subset were computed with that rule, not the one the draft states. Neither rule is wrong; the defect is that the rule actually used was never recorded, so the two are indistinguishable from the artifacts alone. numbers.json now fixes one and prints both n's.

raw_value.verdict: Every quoted correlation that the contract does not reproduce was also searched over 16 alternative (subset, target, unit) conventions. Values still not reproduced under ANY of them cannot be recovered from the archived artifacts and must be regenerated from numbers.json rather than transcribed.

corrections.claim_as_previously_reported: B09 |rho| = 0.766 on the 28-member contract subset

corrected_value.reidentification: This is the single most consequential finding of the audit. Four values the draft presents as correlations of a white-box metric with the ground truth are in fact PAIRED DIFFERENCES against the black-box baseline, computed on a 26-member subset defined by the renderer field. Read as correlations they are wrong by up to 0.67 and one of them has the wrong sign; read as paired differences on that subset they are correct to three decimals. The numbers were never wrong -- their labels were, and no artifact recorded either the quantity or the subset. numbers.json now records both.

corrections.one_sentence_for_the_paper: The 0.766 figure is the 26-member renderer=='chatml' value; the 28-member contract subset the draft attributed it to reads 0.670.

raw_value.conclusion: The falsifier's verdict is UNCHANGED under the convention the draft actually used: no white-box paired advantage over the black-box baseline has a CI excluding zero on this subset either.

raw_value.reidentification_note: This is the single most consequential finding of the audit. Four values the draft presents as correlations of a white-box metric with the ground truth are in fact PAIRED DIFFERENCES against the black-box baseline, computed on a 26-member subset defined by the renderer field. Read as correlations they are wrong by up to 0.67 and one of them has the wrong sign; read as paired differences on that subset they are correct to three decimals. The numbers were never wrong -- their labels were, and no artifact recorded either the quantity or the subset. numbers.json now records both.
raw_value.why: B09's quoted rho of +0.766 is reproduced to 1e-4 on this subset and not on the 28-member member_class subset, so this is the recipe the draft used. The falsifier is re-run here so the conclusion does not depend on which of the two subsets the re-analyst prefers.

raw_value.denominator_finding: the archived ladder records n_harmful = 40 on every row, but the achieved denominators recovered from the rates span 31-40: unparseable judge labels are dropped from the numerator AND the denominator, so the recorded n overstates the evidence behind every rate. Recovery is a SET, not a point -- a rate reducing to a small fraction is compatible with several denominators -- so the largest compatible n is used (the archive requested 40 and dropped only unparseable labels) and the interval implied by the smallest compatible n ships alongside as wilson_*_widest.

corrected_value.power_calculation: two-sided two-proportion z-test, pooled-variance null and unpooled alternative, normal approximation; alpha = 0.05, target power = 0.80, n = 40 per group, baseline p1 = 0.20; grid searched on a 1e-4 step

corrections.one_sentence_for_the_paper: At n = 40 per group and a baseline refusal rate of 0.20, the smallest upward difference detectable with 80% power is 0.29 (i.e. a rate of 0.49) -- so the four signed evasion costs (-0.004, +0.069, +0.075, +0.128) and the int4-minus-root difference (-0.03 [-0.189, +0.135]) are all far below resolution and none of them is a finding.

corrections.one_sentence_for_the_paper: W01 and W04 are retired: on bit-identical weights they differ by 3.1e-2 between two runs, which is the float32 Gram-accumulation floor and not the model, and float64 recomputation moves W01 by exactly the archive gap.

provenance.raw_value: W01/W04 differ by 3.1e-2 on bit-identical weights; float64 moves W01 by 4.7894e-2

corrections.claim_as_previously_reported: W05rel is a new statistic that survives quantization
corrections.one_sentence_for_the_paper: W05rel is retired: it tracks W05 to <0.001 everywhere because the energies are already Frobenius-normalised, so it is the same statistic under another name.

corrections.claim_as_previously_reported: quantization can be undone by dequantizing before scoring

replacement.mechanism: cos(v1,r) stays above 0.999 at EVERY bit width, so the null direction is FILLED IN by rounding noise rather than the eigenvector rotating away; the clean parent is unmoved by the same rounding, so this is not a generic numerical artefact

corrected_value.why: the archived quant_sd was a FAKE-QUANT

corrections.one_sentence_for_the_paper: The proposed dequantization remedy is void -- the archived quantized row was already a dequantized measurement -- and the substantive result in its place is that plain rounding kills the scar at 5 bits (W05 = -2.654, above tau = -2.7415) while refusal is still 0.237 and perplexity moves only 26.25 -> 28.77.

corrections.claim_as_previously_reported: W05 = -4.59 is a property of the edit
corrections.one_sentence_for_the_paper: Storage precision, not the edit, sets the depth of the scar: the SAME complete uniform projection reads W05 = -4.592 stored in bf16 and -12.705 stored in float32, a gap of 8.113 log10 units.

corrections.claim_as_previously_reported: Heretic uses a Gaussian depth kernel (our taxonomy)
corrections.corrected_value: TRIANGULAR TENT WITH A HARD CUTOFF
corrections.one_sentence_for_the_paper: Our own recipe taxonomy was wrong about Heretic: its depth kernel is a triangular tent with a hard cutoff, not a Gaussian, so the R_HERETIC class is not a special case of the Gaussian sweep.

provenance.raw_value: Heretic's per-layer weight is a triangular tent with a hard cutoff

corrections.claim_as_previously_reported: quantized re-uploads are silent false negatives of the scan

corrected_value.handling: excluded by pre-registered eligibility rule E6, status UNRESOLVED or SKIPPED -- never scored and never counted as a negative

corrections.one_sentence_for_the_paper: A quantized upload is UNRESOLVED in the scan pipeline, not a silent false negative: rule E6 excludes it before scoring, so it never enters a rate in either direction.

corrections.claim_as_previously_reported: the parent-free statistic costs nothing relative to a parent-differencing baseline
corrections.one_sentence_for_the_paper: 'Parent-free costs nothing' is retired: on the same rows the parent-differencing E_1 fires on 13/32 while the parent-free W05 fires on 7/35, agreeing on 0.812 of the 32 rows where E_1 is defined at all (0.829 if the 3 rows with no usable parent are counted as E_1 not firing, which is the convention behind the archived 0.829) -- so dropping the parent costs real recall.

corrections.claim_as_previously_reported: a repo-name regex scores 0.727 sensitivity, beating W05's 0.159

corrected_value.status: NAME-SEARCH UPPER BOUND, not a fair baseline

corrections.note: attach as a caveat sentence, not only as a correction
corrections.one_sentence_for_the_paper: The 0.727 regex figure is an UPPER BOUND on a name search, not a fair baseline: the evaluation pool was itself discovered by name sweeps whose terms overlap the regex's own 11 terms, so the regex is scored on a population selected to contain the strings it matches -- this caveat must accompany every place the 0.159-vs-0.727 comparison appears.

raw_value.reading: the regex is trivially spoofable -- an uploader who wants to hide an edit simply renames the repo -- so it is a ceiling on convenience, not on adversarial detection. It is reported because a weights-only detector that does not beat it on ordinary Hub traffic has not earned its complexity.

corrections.claim_as_previously_reported: specificity is 1.000 (0 false positives on 122 eligible undeclared checkpoints)

at_tau_fixed.wilson_formula: centre=(k+z^2/2)/(n+z^2); half=(z/(n+z^2))*sqrt(k*(n-k)/n+z^2/4); interval=[centre-half, centre+half] clipped to [0,1]; z=1.959963984540054; continuity_correction=False

at_tau_refit_modal.wilson_formula: centre=(k+z^2/2)/(n+z^2); half=(z/(n+z^2))*sqrt(k*(n-k)/n+z^2/4); interval=[centre-half, centre+half] clipped to [0,1]; z=1.959963984540054; continuity_correction=False

corrections.one_sentence_for_the_paper: Specificity is a property of the FIXED operating point, not of the statistic: 0/139 eligible undeclared checkpoints fire at tau=-2.7415, but 13/139 fire at the class-held-out refit threshold tau=-1.7156 (rate 0.094, Wilson 95% [0.055, 0.153)]. The narrow honest claim is therefore that zero false positives is achieved AT A THRESHOLD FITTED ON THE PANEL, and does not survive refitting.

corrections.claim_as_previously_reported: the eligible undeclared population is n = 122 (0/122, Wilson [0, 0.031])
corrections.note: this makes the precision claim STRONGER, not weaker -- the denominator grew and the numerator did not
corrections.one_sentence_for_the_paper: The archived 0/122 denominator is a snapshot taken before the newly-fetched scan finished: recounted from the rows now on disk the eligible undeclared population is 139 checkpoints (82 archived + 57 newly scanned), and the false-positive count at the panel operating point is 0, giving 0/139 with Wilson 95% upper bound 0.027.

corrections.claim_as_previously_reported: the abliterated maximum / panel operating point is -2.7415117804

corrected_value.rule: numbers.json must never round -- rounding belongs only in ready-to-paste sentence strings, with the rounding rule stated

corrections.one_sentence_for_the_paper: The iteration-3 numbers file stores the operating point rounded to ten decimal places (-2.7415117804); the full-precision value that the detection rule actually uses is -2.7415117804288127, and every threshold comparison in this paper is made at full precision.

corrections.note: this is the single most consequential correction in the table -- it changes the sign of the reported discrimination on the flipped cells
corrections.one_sentence_for_the_paper: The archived per-class AUROC column reports max(raw, 1 - raw) and records the chosen orientation per cell, so 8 of 19 cells are printed under the OPPOSITE orientation to the detection rule; holding the orientation fixed at lower-is-positive, as the rule W05 <= tau requires, 8 classes fall BELOW chance (ARMB_LAYER_BAND__NONUNIFORM, R_GAUSSIAN_DEPTH, R_GLOBAL_RANK1, R_HERETIC, R_MERGE, R_MULTIDIR_SVD, R_PARTIAL_LAYER, R_SFT_UNCENSORED), which the flipped column hides.
